content:
Apple's highly anticipated AI smart glasses are expected to launch at the end of next year, and finally have a likely debut date.

亮相於 WWDC27

Earlier this year, reports suggested that Apple's AI smart glasses would be available to consumers by the end of 2027. According to a report today by Bloomberg journalist Mark Gurman, that remains the case. However, we now know that Apple is "currently targeting" unveiling the new glasses to the public at next year's Worldwide Developers Conference.

The timing of this unveiling may signal the future direction of Apple's AI glasses. Apple is unlikely to introduce a new device at WWDC without providing developers with any means to create software for it. Therefore, like the all-new Siri AI, the glasses may incorporate third-party app data and actions, rather than being limited to Apple's own features.

If true, the whole process would closely mirror the 2023 launch of the Apple Vision Pro: hardware and software previewed months in advance to let developers build apps for the platform, with the hardware itself going on sale later.

私隱爭議

Apple's glasses have repeatedly slipped from their originally expected end-of-2026 launch date, one reason being the company's ongoing efforts to address privacy concerns. Existing products from companies such as Meta have been heavily criticised, opposed and even banned over concerns about the privacy implications of camera-equipped glasses. According to Gurman's report, Apple is exploring several options. Besides testing a completely camera-less device, Apple is also considering software-based approaches:

In addition, Apple is reportedly "developing new privacy features—both hardware and software-related—that no current product has."

總結

Apple's AI glasses will not feature any display, but are expected to take photos, play music, converse with Siri, take phone calls and perform more functions. The product is also said to sport a distinctive, stylish design to set it apart from competitors. Does this product pique your interest? Let us know in the comments!
